Open the map page

1
Tankers mined near Khasab (29 Oct–1 Nov)
LOUISE 1 hit by limpet mines 25 nm north-east of Khasab and RITI's crew evacuated 1.6 nm off Musandam on 30 Oct; the IRGC says two more tankers exploded on mines on 1 Nov (zone approximate).
2
Tanker hit 72 nm E of Ras Al Khafji (1 Nov)
UKMTO: a south-east-bound tanker was hit on its port side by two projectiles at 23:47 UTC on 1 Nov, about 72 nm east of Ras Al Khafji; crew safe.
3
Hormuz ~14 mb/d (wk to 18 Oct)
Kpler: about 14 mb/d in the week to 18 Oct, 82% of pre-war 17.1 mb/d; Windward counted about 24 AIS-visible crossings from 30 Oct to 1 Nov, up from 18 in the two days before.
4
LNG carrier AL MAYEDA hit (30 Oct)
The Qatari LNG carrier was hit by three projectiles around 18:00 UTC on 30 Oct, about 40 nm south of Lavan Island; no injuries, ship operational.
5
Ras Tanura fire 27 Oct; new Houthi claim 29 Oct
A fire broke out at Saudi Arabia's largest Gulf export terminal after a Houthi missile attack on 27 Oct (contained); on 29 Oct the Houthis claimed new strikes on Ras Tanura and Abqaiq, with no damage confirmed.
6
~492 ships waiting (25 Oct, JMIC)
JMIC counted about 492 vessels waiting outside the strait on 25 Oct; straits.live counted 128 AIS-visible ships holding in the Gulf in its 1 Nov brief, up from 69 on 29 Oct (area approximate).
7
Bypass routes >40% of Gulf exports
Kpler: pipelines avoiding Hormuz carry over 40% of regional exports vs 17% pre-war; East-West line about 5.8 mb/d on 12 Oct; TankerTrackers puts Saudi west-coast exports at 3.32 mb/d in October.
GULF OIL FLOWS · updated 2 Nov 2026

Oil still moves through Hormuz below pre-war: Kpler's latest weekly figure is about 14 mb/d in the week to 18 Oct (82% of the 17.1 mb/d pre-war), while Saudi trackers disagree on October (TankerTrackers ~7.9 mb/d total exports, Kpler 5.7 mb/d). AIS-visible crossings picked up slightly to about 24 between 30 Oct and 1 Nov (Windward), but attacks continued all weekend: limpet mines on the LOUISE 1 25 nm north-east of Khasab, the RITI evacuated off Musandam, the Qatari LNG carrier AL MAYEDA hit 40 nm south of Lavan Island, IRGC claims of two more tankers exploding on mines on 1 Nov, and a tanker hit by two projectiles 72 nm east of Ras Al Khafji late on 1 Nov. Bypass routes still carry over 40% of regional exports, with the Houthis still targeting Saudi export hubs. Diplomacy gained ground this week: Iran and Qatar say Hormuz could reopen within two days if the US meets Tehran's conditions, and Trump reportedly told Netanyahu he wants to give talks more time after the 3 Nov midterms.

Update: Ship attacks continued over the weekend: a tanker was hit by two projectiles 72 nm east of Ras Al Khafji late on 1 Nov, the IRGC says two tankers exploded on mines in Hormuz, and the LNG carrier Al Mayeda was hit 40 nm south of Lavan Island on 30 Oct.

Why it matters: Attacks are spreading into the central and northern Gulf, keeping freight and insurance costs at records and threatening Gulf-side loadings even as diplomacy advances.

Amber · Brent ▼ down · days · medium confidence
Axios: in a 'tough' call on 31 Oct Trump told Netanyahu he wants to give Iran diplomacy more time, while Netanyahu pressed for strikes right after the 3 Nov midterms; Trump said he is not 'in much of a hurry'.
Donald Trump, US President
Why it matters: Lowers the odds of the post-midterm US strike campaign the market had been pricing, cutting the risk premium; Brent fell about 3% at Monday's open. On Sunday Trump still said Iran will 'make a deal, or we'll just end it', so the risk is delayed, not removed.
Trump Gives Iran Diplomacy More Time as Netanyahu Presses for Strikes After US Midterms (Arab Times, citing Axios) · Sat 31 Oct 18:00 UK · Open source
Amber · Brent ▼ down · 1-3 weeks · low confidence
Araghchi says Iran and Qatari mediators reached a proposal under which Hormuz would reopen within two days if the US meets Tehran's conditions (sanctions relief, oil waivers, frozen funds).
Abbas Araghchi, Iran Foreign Minister
“We have reached a proposal at this stage that reduces the implementation period to two days.”
Why it matters: A concrete, short path to reopening Hormuz would sharply cut Brent's war premium; but the conditions are steep and security chief Rezaei says the strait stays closed until all seven are met, so a US yes is far from certain.
